content:
Paper on the bench. White. Stiff.

No name. No stamp. Just a return address in pencil. Smudged. Illegible.

I pick it up. It’s damp. Cold to the touch.

The envelope is thin. Light. But it feels heavy. Wrong.

I tear the seal. Sharp snap.

Inside: one sheet. Folded. Creased deep.

Unfold it. Ink is black. Fresh. Still wet? No. Dried. Days old. Maybe weeks.

Read the words. Short sentences. Blunt facts. Names I know. Dates that don’t fit.

*You were seen.*
*At the pier.*
*3:14 AM.*

My stomach drops. Cold knot. Tightens.

Look around. Empty. Rain hammers the roof. Hides everything.

Fold the paper. Smooth the creases. Put it back in the envelope.

Pocket it. Deep. Against my hip.

Heart beats fast. Hard. Against ribs.

Walk away. Fast. Don’t look back.
